card.decision: When two words tie for longest, should the first one in the text win, or the alphabetically first one?

experts.why: Simplest rule and matches how readers scan text.
Text order is the simplest promise and the one the implementation already keeps.
Matches the natural reading of 'longest word in text' and needs no extra key.
Simpler rule that matches how people read a sentence.

options.consequence: Use max(..., key=len). Docstring states the text-order tie-break; a test asserts the earlier word wins. Simplest code.
options.label: First in text order

options.consequence: Use a key such as (-len(w), w) over the lower-cased words. Docstring states the alphabetical tie-break; a test asserts the alphabetically earlier word wins. Slightly more code. Changing later silently alters results for tied inputs.
options.label: Alphabetically first

ticket.purpose: Add a new module `src/longest.py` with `longest_word(text)` returning the longest word in `text`. Reuse the existing `words` helper from `src/textstats.py`.
ticket.title: Add longest_word

card.while_waiting: This ticket is parked at plan; other tickets continue.
card.why: Ticket 'Add longest_word' reserves this for the owner. max(words(text), key=len) returns the first maximal word, so text order is free. Alphabetical order needs a key such as (-len(w), w) and would compare the lower-cased words that words() returns.
